minutes.headline: Open Space Committee discussed the Townsend Harbor Road parcel but tabled any recommendation vote until March.
minutes.summary: The committee discussed the right of first refusal on a 9.1-acre farmland parcel on Townsend Harbor Road coming out of Chapter. Members and two guests (the agricultural commission chair and a resident) shared views on farmland, a community garden, housing and funding. With only four of seven members present and no formal request for an opinion, they tabled a recommendation vote to the March meeting. January minutes were approved.

attendees.role: guest, chair of the agricultural commission

public_comment.topic: Agricultural commission chair said residents want open space and farming; criteria are hard for large parcels; the parcel may suit APR; a community garden has water and education considerations.

Guest said he will keep acting as watchdog to spread information across committees; 120 days is short to buy without set-aside funds; CPA could assist; assessor is reviewing all Chapter lands; assessed value versus sale price will push up valuations.

what_happened.line: The Open Space Committee tabled any recommendation on the Townsend Harbor Road right of first refusal until its March 12 meeting.
The committee discussed the 9.1-acre farmland parcel leaving Chapter status, with views on farmland, a community garden, housing and funding.
Four of seven members were present and no formal request for an opinion had been made, which figured in the decision to wait.
If the select board acts sooner, the committee would seek a joint meeting with the planning board before March 12.
The chair and guests will ask town counsel whether the agricultural commission could hold land without a town vote.

why_it_matters: A right of first refusal runs on a fixed clock, and a guest noted 120 days is short without a set-aside fund, so waiting a month narrows the time left for any town purchase.
If the town bought the parcel, the money would come from taxes, free cash, grants or Community Preservation Act funds, so the choice affects what residents are asked to approve at town meeting.
